title: GuARD: Effective Anomaly Detection through a Text-Rich and Graph-Informed Language Model

problem.claim: Anomaly detection on text-rich graphs is needed for applications such as identifying incorrectly assigned academic papers and detecting bots in social networks.

gap.claim: Simply introducing rich text into LLMs can obscure essential detection cues and increase fine-tuning costs, while LLMs may overlook graph structural bias important for distinguishing normal from abnormal node patterns.

contributions.claim: GuARD combines key structural features from graph-based methods with fine-grained semantic attributes extracted by small language models for anomaly detection on text-rich graphs.
GuARD uses progressive multimodal multi-turn instruction tuning in a task-guided instruction tuning regime to incorporate rich-text and structural modalities.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on four datasets reportedly show that GuARD outperforms graph-based and LLM-based anomaly detection methods.
On the large-scale WhoIsWho dataset, GuARD reportedly provides up to 5× training speedup and 10× inference speedup over vanilla long-context LLMs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Anomaly detection on text-rich graphs is relevant to real-world applications.
LLM capabilities motivate using rich-text information for anomaly detection.
Existing straightforward LLM use can obscure detection cues, increase fine-tuning costs, and overlook graph structural bias.
GuARD combines graph structural features, semantic attributes from small language models, and progressive multimodal instruction tuning.
The authors report performance and speed advantages across four datasets, including the WhoIsWho dataset.

source_observation.claim: The method combines structural graph features with fine-grained semantic attributes rather than relying on rich text alone.

interpretation.claim: Combining complementary modalities may help preserve anomaly cues that are lost when either text or graph structure is modeled insufficiently.

application.claim: For anomaly detection on text-rich relational data, consider explicitly representing both semantic content and structural patterns.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this multimodal strategy benefits graph domains beyond the reported setting or which component drives the gains.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets beyond WhoIsWho, evaluation metrics, baselines, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not report the absolute performance values or detailed speedup measurement setup.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture, training data, or ablation results.
